### Before cut — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_macro_fov120, macro lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.HW.BUTTON_FACE.R1` (1/1, required)
      120 mm field square-on to the waist button face: full cap, its rim, any maker's
      stamp legible, and the denim seating ring around the shank. Button must fill >=1/3
      of the frame short side. Waistband flat under the button, not tented.
      *why:* The button's stamped face is often the only maker's mark on a garment whose SKU is unknown (DENIM_0001 carries style_sku_unknown), and the button is a second rigid dimensional witness like the rivets. The seating ring records how hard the waistband was compressed, which changes after a wash.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HW.ZIP_PULL.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_zip_fly)
      120 mm field on the slider and pull in the CLOSED position: pull body, slider stamp,
      top stop, and >=40 mm of zip tape with individual teeth resolvable on both chains.
      *why:* Zip tooth pitch is a manufactured constant along the fly, so it is a second independent metric ruler built into the garment, and the slider stamp identifies the hardware maker. Zip tape shrinks differently from denim, which is a known cause of post-wash fly bowing -- unrecorded before the wash, that bowing is indistinguishable from a cutting error.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HW.RIVET_FRONT_L.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_rivets)
      120 mm field, frame long axis along the left front pocket opening. Include BOTH
      terminal rivets if the opening's rivet-to-rivet span is under 100 mm; otherwise the
      upper rivet alone and emit the lower as .R2. The rivet cap must fill >=1/3 of the
      frame's short side; cap rim, stamped face and the compressed denim ring around the
      burr all in focus.
      *why:* Rivets are the only rigid, dimensionally stable objects sewn into the garment, so they are the internal scale check that survives the wash unchanged -- if the rivet's measured diameter changes between before and post-wash, the scale chain is wrong, not the garment. The compressed denim ring around the burr is also the first place local shrinkage shows.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HW.RIVET_FRONT_R.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_rivets)
      Mirror of RIVET_FRONT_L on the right front pocket opening: 120 mm field, rivet cap
      >=1/3 of the frame short side, cap rim and stamped face in focus.
      *why:* Second independent rigid scale witness; two rivets on opposite sides let the scale check be done per-side, catching a tilt that a single rivet would absorb into an apparent diameter change.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HW.RIVET_COIN.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_watch_pocket_rivets)
      120 mm field on the coin-pocket rivet pair: both rivets if their span is under 100
      mm, cap rim and stamped face in focus, the coin pocket's top hem crossing the frame
      for location.
      *why:* Coin-pocket rivets sit on the thickest ply stack on the garment, so they are where rivet-to-denim differential movement is largest; they also date and identify the construction. Without them the coin pocket's corners have no rigid reference.

### Before cut — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_macro_fov150_tex, macro lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.TEX.FRONT_L_UPPER.R1` (1/1, required)
      150 mm field on the left front leg, 100 mm below the crotch junction, midway between
      inseam and outseam. The frame must contain a >=100 x 100 mm patch of continuous body
      weave with NO seam, hardware, print, fade edge or pocket bag inside it. Fabric flat
      and un-stretched; camera perpendicular to the fabric plane.
      *why:* GATE_TEX derivation: a denim warp yarn is roughly 0.4-0.6 mm wide. Two pixels per yarn is only the Nyquist limit -- it detects the twill periodicity but cannot separate a yarn from its neighbour. Eight pixels across the NARROWEST yarn (0.4 mm) is what lets the twill diagonal be traced and a yarn width be measured, giving 0.4/8 = 0.05 mm/px as the ceiling. On a 4032 px long edge that is a 200 mm field; specifying 150 mm leaves margin and lands near 0.037 mm/px, about 11 px per 0.4 mm yarn. The 100 mm clean patch is exactly four ChArUco squares (25.0 mm, protocol/charuco_board.json), so it is directly comparable to a board-scaled measurement. Without this the post-wash weave comparison has no before-state at a scale where shrinkage-driven yarn crowding is visible at all.
- [ ] `BEFORE.TEX.FRONT_L_MID.R1` (1/2, required)
      150 mm field on the left front leg at the knee position (crotch +
      original_inseam_cm/2 = 381 mm for DENIM_0001), midway between inseam and outseam,
      containing a >=100 x 100 mm clean weave patch free of seams, hardware and fade
      edges. Fabric flat and un-stretched.
      *why:* The mid-leg weave patch is the reference sample for the whole fabric, and the two-repetition FULL RE-LAY pair is the only measurement in the catalogue that bounds weave-metric repeatability from below as well as above. EXP_0021's warning is exactly that simulated re-captures cannot move the fabric and so flatter the error estimate; without a real re-lay pair every post-wash weave delta has an unknown noise floor.
- [ ] `BEFORE.TEX.FRONT_L_MID.R1` (2/2, required)  **TAKE THE PHONE OFF THE MOUNT AND REMOUNT IT**
      150 mm field on the left front leg at the knee position (crotch +
      original_inseam_cm/2 = 381 mm for DENIM_0001), midway between inseam and outseam,
      containing a >=100 x 100 mm clean weave patch free of seams, hardware and fade
      edges. Fabric flat and un-stretched.
      *why:* The mid-leg weave patch is the reference sample for the whole fabric, and the two-repetition FULL RE-LAY pair is the only measurement in the catalogue that bounds weave-metric repeatability from below as well as above. EXP_0021's warning is exactly that simulated re-captures cannot move the fabric and so flatter the error estimate; without a real re-lay pair every post-wash weave delta has an unknown noise floor.
- [ ] `BEFORE.TEX.FRONT_R_MID.R1` (1/1, required)
      Mirror of TEX.FRONT_L_MID on the right front leg at the 381 mm knee position: 150 mm
      field, >=100 x 100 mm clean weave patch, fabric flat and un-stretched.
      *why:* Cross-leg weave comparison at the same height. Denim is cut from a roll with warp running along the leg, and the two legs can come from different roll positions; without a matched right-leg patch, an L/R difference after the wash cannot be attributed to the treatment rather than to the fabric.
- [ ] `BEFORE.TEX.FRONT_L_LOWER.R1` (1/1, required)
      150 mm field on the left front leg at 3/4 of original_inseam_cm from the crotch (572
      mm for DENIM_0001), midway between inseam and outseam, containing a >=100 x 100 mm
      clean weave patch. Fabric flat and un-stretched.
      *why:* Lower-leg weave is the least abraded fabric on the garment and is where PROTOCOL SS0 already puts the caliper for fabric_thickness_mm, so it pairs a visual weave record with a physical thickness reading. It is also the offcut's own weave baseline, without which the offcut's post-wash weave has nothing to be compared to.

### Before cut — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_macro_fov200, main lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.WAIST.CLOSURE_BUTTON.R1` (1/1, required)
      Fly closed, lying naturally. 200 mm field centred on the waist closure so the
      button, its buttonhole (and any second hole of a double closure) and the full
      waistband height at that point are all inside, with >=40 mm of waistband either
      side.
      *why:* Gives a lay-invariant shrinkage measurand (button centre to buttonhole centre) plus the buttonhole bar-tack condition. Without it, waist shrinkage can only be estimated from a soft flat-laid edge whose length depends on how hard the operator smoothed it.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WAIST.CROTCH_SEAM_FRONT.R1` (1/1, required)
      200 mm field centred on the four-way junction where the fly bottom, the two front
      leg panels and the two inseams meet: >=70 mm of each inseam radiating down-left and
      down-right, the fly bottom bar-tack at the top, all crotch reinforcement stitch rows
      complete and unclipped.
      *why:* The front crotch is the origin of the inseam measurement and the single highest-ply junction on the garment, so it fixes where every inseam-referenced length starts and is where wash pucker appears first. At the 550 mm rise framing the junction is a few dozen pixels and the ply structure is unreadable.
- [ ] `BEFORE.POCKET.COIN.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_coin_pocket)
      200 mm field: the whole coin/watch pocket including both upper corners, its full
      hem, every stitch row and any rivets, plus >=40 mm of the front pocket opening it
      sits inside so its position is recoverable.
      *why:* The coin pocket is a small, sharply bounded, four-to-six-ply patch on an otherwise two-ply field, so it is the most sensitive local shrinkage witness on the garment. It is also the feature most often absent, which is why its shot is conditional rather than required.

### Before cut — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_mid_overhead_hem, main lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.FRONT_COMPLETE.OVERHEAD` (1/1, required)
      Garment front-up, left leg laid straight and smoothed. Frame the complete front-
      panel hem edge from the inseam seam to the outseam, plus 120 mm of leg above the
      hem, plus the ChArUco board lying flat in the same corner of the frame as always.
      The hem edge must run end to end across the frame with at least 20 mm of backdrop
      beyond both seam ends. The certified loop tape lies on the surface parallel to and
      about 10 mm outboard of the hem edge, zero at the inseam seam, graduations legible.
      *why:* The original factory hem is the project's own finished-edge negative control: a hemmed edge does not fray however it is washed (CONTRIBUTING_PAIRS.md), and hem_roughness's published negative control is exactly a finished hem (EXP_0024). This frame records that control's geometry at a scale where fray would be visible if it existed, and it is the board-bearing metric anchor for the left leg's hem region. It is also the last chance to record this edge: after the cut the original hem leaves the garment on the offcut and can never be rephotographed in situ.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.RIGHT.FRONT_COMPLETE.OVERHEAD` (1/1, required)
      As BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.FRONT_COMPLETE.OVERHEAD but for the right leg (wearer's right,
      i.e. the leg on the viewer's left when the garment lies front-up). Same mount
      height, same board corner of the frame, same tape offset, same lens and crop, so the
      two legs are directly comparable.
      *why:* Per-leg finished-hem control. The two legs are not interchangeable evidence: PROTOCOL section 7 assigns different wash conditions to the L and R offcuts, so each leg's original hem must be documented separately or the scrap-vs-garment control loses its baseline.

### Before cut — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_overhead_fov350, main lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.WAIST.FLY_ZIP.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_zip_fly)
      Fly closed. 350 mm field, long axis vertical, fly topstitch curve down the frame
      centre: waistband lower seam in the top 15%, the fly's bottom bar-tack >=60 mm above
      the frame bottom, full topstitch width plus 60 mm of front panel either side.
      *why:* The fly is the front rise's structural spine and the one place where a metal component is sewn through several plies; its topstitch curve is the front-panel registration curve. Losing it removes the only rigid front reference between waistband and crotch.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WAIST.FLY_BUTTON.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_button_fly)
      Fly closed. 350 mm field, long axis vertical: every fly button and its buttonhole in
      one column, the placket edge, the waistband seam in the top 15%, the bottom bar-tack
      >=60 mm above the frame bottom.
      *why:* Button-fly spacing is a fixed ladder of inter-landmark distances down the front rise, giving several independent shrinkage readings from one frame. Without it a button-fly garment has no rigid front reference at all.
- [ ] `BEFORE.POCKET.FRONT_OPENING_L.R1` (1/1, required)
      350 mm field with the whole pocket opening curve running corner-to-corner across the
      frame from the waistband seam to the side seam; both terminal rivets or bar-tacks
      inside with >=40 mm of denim beyond each; the pocket bag edge included if it shows
      through.
      *why:* The front pocket opening is a curve of known construction whose two ends are rivets -- a rigid two-point span plus a shape. It is also the boundary of a double-ply region that shrinks differently from the single-ply panel beside it, which is the mechanism behind post-wash front-panel pucker.
- [ ] `BEFORE.POCKET.FRONT_OPENING_R.R1` (1/1, required)
      Mirror of FRONT_OPENING_L: 350 mm field, whole right pocket opening curve corner-to-
      corner, both terminal rivets/bar-tacks with >=40 mm of denim beyond each.
      *why:* Right-hand counterpart, and half of the only L/R symmetry evidence on the front panel; the coin pocket sits inside one of the two and biases its ply count.
- [ ] `BEFORE.LEG.KNEE_L.R1` (1/1, required)
      350 mm field centred on the left knee position (crotch + original_inseam_cm/2 along
      the inseam = 381 mm for DENIM_0001): full leg width plus >=30 mm of backdrop each
      side, the whole knee fade/whiskering pattern inside the frame.
      *why:* The knee is the most heavily abraded region on a worn pair and DENIM_0001 records knee fades explicitly; because a jorts cut removes it, this is the last chance to record it as part of the garment rather than as scrap. It becomes the offcut's identity anchor.
- [ ] `BEFORE.LEG.SHIN_L.R1` (1/1, required)
      350 mm field centred midway between the left knee position and the hem, i.e. 3/4 of
      original_inseam_cm from the crotch (572 mm for DENIM_0001): full leg width plus >=30
      mm of backdrop each side.
      *why:* The shin is the least-abraded part of the leg, so it is the closest thing on this garment to unworn reference fabric, and it is the region the offcut is mostly made of. PROTOCOL SS0 already specifies fabric thickness is measured on the lower leg, so this frame is the visual record beside that caliper reading.
- [ ] `BEFORE.LEG.KNEE_R.R1` (1/1, required)
      Mirror of KNEE_L: 350 mm field centred on the right knee position (381 mm from the
      crotch along the inseam), full leg width plus >=30 mm of backdrop each side.
      *why:* Right knee counterpart; the L/R fade pair is the strongest evidence of wear asymmetry, and asymmetric wear is the leading candidate explanation for asymmetric post-wash fray.
- [ ] `BEFORE.LEG.SHIN_R.R1` (1/1, required)
      Mirror of SHIN_L: 350 mm field centred 572 mm from the crotch on the right leg, full
      leg width plus >=30 mm of backdrop each side.
      *why:* Right shin reference fabric. Under PROTOCOL SS7 the two offcuts receive different wash conditions, so this frame and SHIN_L are the paired baselines for the repeat-wash noise sample; without both, the scrap-vs-garment control has only one arm.
- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.INTERSECT_HEM_L.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_factory_hem)
      350 mm field, long axis HORIZONTAL across the left leg opening: the whole factory
      hem line from the outseam termination to the inseam termination, the hem's turn-up
      stitch row unbroken across the full width, and >=60 mm of leg above the hem.
      *why:* The factory hem is the finished-edge NEGATIVE CONTROL for the entire fray question: eval/hem_texture's own validation turned on distinguishing a frayed hem from a finished one, and without a before-state finished hem on this exact fabric there is nothing to contrast the post-wash cut edge against. It also carries both hem seam intersections in one frame.
- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.INTERSECT_HEM_R.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_factory_hem)
      Mirror of INTERSECT_HEM_L: 350 mm field horizontally across the right leg opening,
      whole factory hem line outseam-to-inseam, stitch row unbroken, >=60 mm of leg above
      the hem.
      *why:* Second finished-edge control, on the offcut that receives the OTHER SS7 wash condition. One control is not enough when the two offcuts are washed differently, because the control has to be paired with its own treatment arm.

### Before cut — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_overhead_fov550, main lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.WAIST.WAISTBAND_FRONT.R1` (1/2, required)
      Garment front-up. 550 mm field, long axis horizontal. Whole waistband as a strip:
      top edge at 15% down the frame, strip bottom 40 mm below the waistband's lower seam
      so pocket-top and fly-top junctions are inside; both side-seam ends >=30 mm inside
      the left/right frame edges.
      *why:* The waistband is the only landmark that survives the cut unchanged, so it is the before/after registration anchor and the shrinkage measurand. Two repetitions with a FULL RE-LAY are the only honest re-lay noise floor for this framing; EXP_0021 warns that simulated re-captures cannot move the fabric and therefore bound error from above only. Without it every later before/after delta silently carries lay variance.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WAIST.BELT_LOOPS_FRONT.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_belt_loops)
      550 mm field on the front waistband: every front and side-front belt loop inside
      with BOTH its top and bottom bar-tacks visible, 40 mm of waistband above and below,
      loops lying flat and unfolded (unfold by hand before shooting).
      *why:* Belt loops are discrete, evenly spaced, high-contrast fiducials along the waistband -- the best available landmark set for measuring differential shrinkage ALONG the waist rather than across it. Folded loops in the main waistband frame make those spacings unmeasurable.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WAIST.RISE_FRONT.R1` (1/1, required)
      550 mm field, long axis VERTICAL: top of the waistband in the top 10% of the frame,
      the front crotch-seam junction >=60 mm above the frame bottom, full fly width plus
      the inner edge of both front pocket openings.
      *why:* This frame must contain the entire front_rise_cm measurand (waistband top to crotch seam) in ONE image, so the rise can be re-measured from pixels after the wash without stitching two frames. PROTOCOL requires two readings per dimension; a rise split across frames cannot be re-derived at all.
- [ ] `BEFORE.LEG.THIGH_FRONT_L.R1` (1/1, required)
      550 mm field, long axis vertical along the left leg, garment front-up: the
      crotch/inseam junction in the top 10%, frame bottom >=80 mm below the knee position
      (crotch + original_inseam_cm/2 = 381 mm for DENIM_0001's 76.2 cm inseam); BOTH the
      outseam and inseam of that leg inside with >=40 mm of backdrop beyond the outseam.
      *why:* The thigh panel is where the jorts cut lands, so the before-state weave, whiskering and seam geometry of the RETAINED panel is the single most consequential pre-cut record in the catalogue; DENIM_0001's existing_damage_annotations put pronounced whiskering exactly here. Once the shears close this frame cannot be retaken.
- [ ] `BEFORE.LEG.THIGH_FRONT_R.R1` (1/1, required)
      Mirror of THIGH_FRONT_L on the right leg: 550 mm field, crotch junction in the top
      10%, frame bottom >=80 mm below the 381 mm knee position, both seams of that leg
      inside.
      *why:* Right-hand retained panel. The L/R pair is the only before-state evidence that lets differential shrinkage be separated from a cut that was not symmetric, which is otherwise the single most likely confound in this whole experiment.

### Before cut — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_overhead_locked, main lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.WHOLE.F00.NULL` (1/2, required)
      Two frames of the F00 framing taken back to back with NOTHING touched between them —
      not the garment, not the mount, not the lights, not a setting. Press the shutter,
      wait, press it again. This is additional to the five relay captures and does not
      count as one of them.
      *why:* The noise floor, and it is not a formality. EXP_0021 found that re-encoding one photograph at JPEG 15 changes hem roughness by 80% of its own value with nothing in the scene having moved, and that the fray verdict flips on 6 of 16 photographs under perturbations that touch no fabric at all. Without this pair, the re-lay and remount spreads have nothing to be compared against and could be entirely encoder noise. It costs one minute.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WHOLE.F00.R1` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 F00. Garment front-up, waistband at the top of frame, legs spread to the
      frozen gap and aligned to the RIG.LAY.GAP_TEMPLATE marks, smoothed by hand, no pins.
      Whole garment inside the frame with visible backdrop on all four sides — no part of
      the garment may touch a frame edge. Board flat in its frozen corner, entirely
      outside the garment's bounding box. Camera untouched on the mount; exposure and
      white balance still locked at the session values.
      *why:* The primary measurement frame of the entire project: the front silhouette from which the landmarks, the shape ratios and the cut line are all derived, and the source of record for capture_mm_per_px and capture_board_corners. Rep 1 of the relay-only arm — the camera is not touched across R1, R2 and R3, so their spread isolates the variance contributed by laying the fabric out again, which is the component this project has never once measured and the reason PROTOCOL §6 exists.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WHOLE.F00.R2` (1/1, required)
      Identical to BEFORE.WHOLE.F00.R1. Before shooting: lift the garment completely clear
      of the backdrop, shake it out, and lay it down again from scratch to the frozen gap
      marks. Do not adjust the mount, the exposure or the white balance.
      *why:* Rep 2 of the relay-only arm. Its only difference from R1 is the fabric, which is precisely the point: every tolerance this project currently quotes comes from simulated re-captures that, in EXP_0021's own words, cannot move the fabric, change the drape or move the light, and therefore bound the error from above and no more.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WHOLE.F00.R3` (1/1, required)
      Identical to BEFORE.WHOLE.F00.R1, with another complete lift-and-relay first.
      Camera, exposure and white balance still untouched since R1.
      *why:* Rep 3 completes the relay-only arm at n=3, which is 2 degrees of freedom on the re-lay variance. That is a bound, not an estimate, and it is a direct consequence of PROTOCOL §6 specifying five captures in total; the arithmetic should be stated in the report rather than the spread quoted as if it were a standard deviation.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WHOLE.F00.R4` (1/1, required)
      Identical framing to BEFORE.WHOLE.F00.R1, reached differently: FIRST take the phone
      off the mount entirely and set it down, THEN lift and re-lay the garment, THEN
      remount the phone and re-establish the framing against the on-screen guide and the
      board's frozen corner. Re-apply the exposure and white-balance lock at the session
      values.
      *why:* Rep 4 opens the relay-plus-reposition arm. R1-R3 hold the camera fixed and therefore cannot see rig variance at all, yet every real comparison in this project — before against immediate_after against post_wash, taken hours or weeks apart — involves a camera that has been touched. Without at least one arm that includes a remount, the quoted repeatability would systematically understate the error of exactly the comparison the project is built on. R4 and R5 are the reposition arm because the fabric component is the unmeasured one and gets the larger share of a five-capture budget.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WHOLE.F00.R5` (1/1, required)
      As BEFORE.WHOLE.F00.R4: dismount the phone, re-lay the garment from scratch,
      remount, re-establish framing and locks, shoot.
      *why:* Rep 5 completes PROTOCOL §6's five captures and gives the reposition arm a second point, so that arm has a spread at all rather than a single value. Together R1-R5 are the first physical repeatability data this project has ever held; everything before them is simulated.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WHOLE.F00.STRETCH_SETTLE` (1/1, conditional, is_stretch)
      Exactly the BEFORE.WHOLE.F00.R1 framing, repeated after the garment has been left
      undisturbed on the backdrop for the frozen settle interval. Do not touch the
      garment, the mount or any setting during the interval.
      *why:* Elastane recovers over minutes after handling, so a stretch garment's silhouette is still changing while the five reps are being taken and the re-lay variance those reps measure would be contaminated by a monotonic drift that is not re-lay variance at all. This frame is what separates the two. It is conditional because a 0% elastane garment has no such drift — DENIM_0001 is 100% cotton and would skip it.

### Before cut — FRONT up, lay 1, oblique_station_30deg, main lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.OBLIQUE.FL1` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 FL1. Stand at the taped FRONT-LEFT station (the garment's left side,
      which is the image-RIGHT side of the front-up lay). Garment front-up in the F00 lay,
      undisturbed. Hold the phone with its long axis parallel to the leg's centre line and
      the optical axis at about 30 degrees from the surface normal, tilted ACROSS the leg
      toward your station, aimed at the centre of leg section 1 — the midpoint of the
      topmost quarter of the crotch-to-hem length, i.e. 0.125 of the inseam below the
      crotch seam. Step in until the leg's cross-width fills the on-screen guide (about a
      quarter of the frame's short dimension). Both the outseam and the inseam edge of the
      section must be in frame with at least 50 mm of backdrop beyond each, and the
      ChArUco board must be in frame, flat on the backdrop beside the framed section.
      *why:* The overhead frames record the silhouette and destroy the surface: flat frontal light on flat fabric shows no relief. A 30 degree oblique across the leg rakes the light, which is the only way seam relief, weave direction, residual drape and the topology of a fade become visible. Section 1 is the topmost quarter, above any plausible jorts cut line, so it is the one leg section that stays on the garment through the cut and is directly comparable across all three garment states.
- [ ] `BEFORE.OBLIQUE.FL2` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 FL2. As FL1 from the same FRONT-LEFT station, aimed at the centre of leg
      section 2 — 0.375 of the inseam below the crotch seam. Same 30 degree axis, same
      fill in the guide, board in frame beside the section.
      *why:* Section 2 straddles the region where a jorts cut typically lands, so it is the section most likely to contain the cut line itself. Its before-state oblique is therefore the surface record of the fabric immediately either side of the future cut — the fabric whose weave and fade will be interrupted by it — captured while it is still continuous.
- [ ] `BEFORE.OBLIQUE.FL3` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 FL3. As FL1 from the FRONT-LEFT station, aimed at the centre of leg
      section 3 — 0.625 of the inseam below the crotch seam. Same 30 degree axis, same
      guide fill, board in frame.
      *why:* Section 3 is knee-region fabric that becomes part of the offcut. Under PROTOCOL §7 the offcuts carry a raw edge identical to the garment's and are washed under an assigned condition, and §5 says their fray is measured exactly as the garment's — so they are experimental subjects, not scrap. This is the only before-cut surface record of the fabric they are made of, and without it the offcut fray results have no baseline.
- [ ] `BEFORE.OBLIQUE.FL4` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 FL4. As FL1 from the FRONT-LEFT station, aimed at the centre of leg
      section 4 — 0.875 of the inseam below the crotch seam. The original hem edge must be
      inside the frame with at least 50 mm of backdrop below it. Same 30 degree axis, same
      guide fill, board in frame.
      *why:* Section 4 carries the original factory hem and becomes the offcut's finished end. Photographed obliquely before anything is cut, it records how this fabric behaves at a finished edge under raking light, which is the appearance the raw cut edge will later be compared against. It also completes the four-section coverage of the leg so the sections overlap and no band of fabric goes unrecorded.
- [ ] `BEFORE.OBLIQUE.FR1` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 FR1. Stand at the taped FRONT-RIGHT station (the garment's right side,
      which is the image-LEFT side of the front-up lay). Garment front-up in the F00 lay,
      undisturbed. Optical axis about 30 degrees from the surface normal, tilted across
      the leg toward your station, aimed at the centre of leg section 1 (0.125 of the
      inseam below the crotch seam). Leg cross-width fills the guide; outseam and inseam
      edges plus 50 mm of backdrop beyond each in frame; board in frame beside the
      section.
      *why:* The mirror of FL1 on the leg that will be cut second. PROTOCOL §3.4 cuts the legs separately, so the two legs are two independent trials of the same cut, and each needs its own before-state surface record for its result to mean anything on its own.
- [ ] `BEFORE.OBLIQUE.FR2` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 FR2. As FR1 from the FRONT-RIGHT station, aimed at the centre of leg
      section 2 (0.375 of the inseam below the crotch seam).
      *why:* The right leg's cut-region section, mirroring FL2. Since PROTOCOL §7 assigns the two offcuts to different wash conditions, the two legs' cut-region records are not redundant: they are the before states of two differently treated experimental units.
- [ ] `BEFORE.OBLIQUE.FR3` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 FR3. As FR1 from the FRONT-RIGHT station, aimed at the centre of leg
      section 3 (0.625 of the inseam below the crotch seam).
      *why:* The right offcut's knee-region baseline. PROTOCOL §7 makes the two offcuts a wash-condition contrast (one in the garment's load, one in a separate standard load), so each offcut needs its own before-state fabric record for that contrast to be interpretable.
- [ ] `BEFORE.OBLIQUE.FR4` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 FR4. As FR1 from the FRONT-RIGHT station, aimed at the centre of leg
      section 4 (0.875 of the inseam below the crotch seam), with the original hem edge
      and 50 mm of backdrop below it in frame.
      *why:* Completes the right front leg's four-section coverage and records its original hem obliquely. The two legs' hems are the two halves of the asymmetry check, and any pre-existing difference between them must be on record before the cut, because after the cut a left/right difference cannot be attributed between the garment and the cutting.

### Before cut — either face, lay 1, handheld_raking_30, main lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.HEM_CURL_L.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_factory_hem and has_hem_curl_visible)
      Camera handheld at ~30 degrees to the fabric plane, sighting ALONG the left hem line
      from the outseam end toward the inseam end, so the hem edge is seen edge-on against
      the backdrop; the whole hem line in frame with the highest lift point at frame
      centre.
      *why:* Edge curl is a named PROTOCOL SS5 post-wash measurand (max vertical lift of the hem edge from the surface). A before-state reading on the FACTORY hem is the only control that distinguishes curl created by the wash from curl the garment already had; without it, any post-wash curl number is uninterpretable.

### Before cut — either face, lay 1, mount_grazing_table, tele lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.EDGE_PROFILE.SIDE` (1/1, required)
      Garment front-up and conditioned flat. Camera at the grazing station: optical axis
      in the surface plane, horizontal, perpendicular to the left leg's front-panel hem
      edge, looking at the hem from beyond the leg opening. A vertical steel rule stands
      on the surface at the frame centre, zero touching the surface, just outside the
      fabric. Frame about 100 mm of hem edge in silhouette against a plain dark card
      standing behind the leg. The stacked front-panel and back-panel edges must both be
      distinguishable in silhouette; the surface line must be visible across the frame.
      *why:* Two measurements at once, neither of which survives the cut: the original hem's total thickness in fabric layers (an independent check on the schema's fabric_thickness_mm, which PROTOCOL section 0.4 otherwise takes from a caliper on a single layer), and the finished hem's baseline edge curl. A finished hem's curl is the zero point against which the post-wash cut edge's curl is read; without it, a post-wash curl number has nothing to be a change from.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.SIDE_CURL.P01` (1/1, required)
      PARAMETERISED SERIES sharing the macro centres. For each centre index c the
      generator emits one instance with Pnn replaced by the zero-padded index. Grazing
      station: optical axis in the surface plane, horizontal, perpendicular to the local
      edge tangent at position Pc, dark card standing behind the leg, vertical steel rule
      stood on the surface at the frame centre with its zero touching the surface. Frame
      about 100 mm of edge in silhouette so that positions Pc-2 .. Pc+2 are all inside the
      frame. Front-up lay only; do not re-lay, smooth or lift the garment anywhere in the
      series.  [frame 1 of 6 around the loop: arc 0-76 mm from the inseam seam, covering
      measurement position(s) 1, 2]
      *why:* Baseline edge curl of the finished hem around the loop, in the geometry PROTOCOL section 5 defines (garment laid front-up, max vertical lift of the edge from the surface). A finished hem's curl is small but not zero, and the post-wash cut-edge curl is only interpretable as a change against it.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.SIDE_CURL.P02` (1/1, required)
      PARAMETERISED SERIES sharing the macro centres. For each centre index c the

      edge tangent at position Pc, dark card standing behind the leg, vertical steel rule

      about 100 mm of edge in silhouette so that positions Pc-2 .. Pc+2 are all inside the
      frame. Front-up lay only; do not re-lay, smooth or lift the garment anywhere in the
      series.  [frame 6 of 6 around the loop: arc 380-456 mm from the inseam seam,
      covering measurement position(s) 1, 2]
      *why:* Baseline edge curl of the finished hem around the loop, in the geometry PROTOCOL section 5 defines (garment laid front-up, max vertical lift of the edge from the surface). A finished hem's curl is small but not zero, and the post-wash cut-edge curl is only interpretable as a change against it.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.RIGHT.EDGE_PROFILE.SIDE` (1/1, required)
      As BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.EDGE_PROFILE.SIDE but for the right leg, same station geometry
      and vertical rule placement.
      *why:* Per-leg thickness and baseline curl, for the same reason as the left leg.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.RIGHT.SIDE_CURL.P01` (1/1, required)
      As BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.SIDE_CURL.Pnn but for the right leg, using the right leg's own
      centre indices.  [frame 1 of 6 around the loop: arc 0-76 mm from the inseam seam,
      covering measurement position(s) 1, 2]
      *why:* Per-leg baseline curl, for the same reason as the left leg.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.RIGHT.SIDE_CURL.P02` (1/1, required)
      As BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.SIDE_CURL.Pnn but for the right leg, using the right leg's own
      centre indices.  [frame 2 of 6 around the loop: arc 76-152 mm from the inseam seam,
      covering measurement position(s) 3, 4]
      *why:* Per-leg baseline curl, for the same reason as the left leg.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.RIGHT.SIDE_CURL.P03` (1/1, required)
      As BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.SIDE_CURL.Pnn but for the right leg, using the right leg's own
      centre indices.  [frame 3 of 6 around the loop: arc 152-228 mm from the inseam seam,
      covering measurement position(s) 5, 6]
      *why:* Per-leg baseline curl, for the same reason as the left leg.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.RIGHT.SIDE_CURL.P04` (1/1, required)
      As BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.SIDE_CURL.Pnn but for the right leg, using the right leg's own
      centre indices.  [frame 4 of 6 around the loop: arc 228-304 mm from the inseam seam,
      covering measurement position(s) 7, 8]
      *why:* Per-leg baseline curl, for the same reason as the left leg.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.RIGHT.SIDE_CURL.P05` (1/1, required)
      As BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.SIDE_CURL.Pnn but for the right leg, using the right leg's own
      centre indices.  [frame 5 of 6 around the loop: arc 304-380 mm from the inseam seam,
      covering measurement position(s) 9, 10]
      *why:* Per-leg baseline curl, for the same reason as the left leg.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.RIGHT.SIDE_CURL.P06` (1/1, required)
      As BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.SIDE_CURL.Pnn but for the right leg, using the right leg's own
      centre indices.  [frame 6 of 6 around the loop: arc 380-456 mm from the inseam seam,
      covering measurement position(s) 1, 2]
      *why:* Per-leg baseline curl, for the same reason as the left leg.

### Before cut — either face, lay 1, mount_macro_fov120, macro lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.HW.DECOR.I01.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_decorative_hardware)
      120 mm field on decorative hardware instance NN as enumerated at intake: the whole
      item, its full attachment to the fabric, and >=30 mm of surrounding denim. Garment
      face is bound at instantiation from the intake entry's location field and written
      into the manifest.
      *why:* Decorative hardware is the least predictable component in a wash (plating loss, rust bleed onto adjacent denim) and is entirely garment-specific, so a generic shot cannot stand in for it. One frame per instance is the only way the post-wash comparison has a matching before frame.

### Before cut — either face, lay 1, mount_macro_fov150_tex, macro lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.SELVEDGE_L.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_selvedge)
      120 mm field on the left outseam gently opened flat BY HAND (never stretched): the
      woven selvedge edge running the full length of the frame, the ID line's colour and
      any lettering, and >=30 mm of body fabric inboard so the selvedge-to-body weave
      transition is visible.
      *why:* The selvedge band is a woven edge that cannot fray and whose ID yarn count is a manufacturing constant, so it is both a fabric-identity fingerprint and a second in-fabric dimensional witness independent of the rivets. It also shows the weave at the loom's own edge, where warp density differs from the body -- the reference the body TEX shots are compared against.
- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.SELVEDGE_R.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_selvedge)
      Mirror of SELVEDGE_L on the right outseam, gently opened flat by hand: selvedge band
      the full frame length, ID line legible, >=30 mm of body fabric inboard.
      *why:* Right selvedge; each leg is cut from a different part of the roll, so the two ID bands are the check on whether the two legs are even the same fabric lot -- which, if they are not, changes every symmetric-shrinkage assumption in the experiment.

### Before cut — either face, lay 1, mount_macro_fov200, main lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.WAIST.WAISTBAND_CORNER_L.R1` (1/1, required)
      200 mm field on the junction where the left waistband end, the outseam and the
      front/back panels meet. Waistband top edge across the upper third; >=60 mm of
      outseam below the corner and >=60 mm of waistband inboard; nearest belt loop
      included if present.
      *why:* The waistband corner is the highest-stress junction on the garment and the fixed end-point of the waist circumference; wash shrinkage shows first as pucker at this bar-tack. At the 550 mm waistband framing the bar-tack is a smudge, so without this frame the shrinkage mechanism is unobservable.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WAIST.WAISTBAND_CORNER_R.R1` (1/1, required)
      Mirror of WAISTBAND_CORNER_L: 200 mm field on the right waistband end / outseam
      junction, >=60 mm of outseam below and >=60 mm of waistband inboard.
      *why:* Right-hand counterpart; the L/R pair is the only evidence of construction asymmetry at the waist, which otherwise gets read post-wash as differential shrinkage.
- [ ] `BEFORE.ANOM.DISTRESS.R1.I01` (1/1, conditional, n_distressing > 0)
      200 mm field centred on distressing instance NN as enumerated in the record's
      existing_damage_annotations; the whole feature plus >=40 mm of undamaged denim on
      every side, and the nearest seam or hardware landmark inside the frame so the
      feature is relocatable. If the feature is longer than 160 mm, shoot overlapping
      frames R1..Rn with >=30% overlap. Garment face is bound at instantiation from the
      annotation's location field.
      *why:* Pre-existing distressing is loose or broken weave that will fray in the wash independently of anything the shears do, so an unrecorded instance becomes a false positive in the post-wash fray measurement. One frame per instance is the only way each is separately attributable.
- [ ] `BEFORE.ANOM.TEAR.R1.I01` (1/1, conditional, n_tears > 0)
      200 mm field centred on tear instance NN: the full extent of the tear including both
      terminations, >=40 mm of intact denim beyond each, any exposed weft floats, and the
      nearest seam landmark. Do not open, close or flatten the tear -- shoot it as it
      lies.
      *why:* A tear grows in a wash and its terminations migrate, so its before-state length and end-points are the only way to say afterwards whether it grew. Unrecorded, a grown tear is indistinguishable from wash-induced damage the protocol would have to explain.
- [ ] `BEFORE.ANOM.REPAIR.R1.I01` (1/1, conditional, n_repairs > 0)
      200 mm field centred on repair instance NN: the whole repair, every repair stitch
      row, the boundary between repair thread and original fabric, >=40 mm of intact denim
      on each side, and the nearest seam landmark.
      *why:* Repair thread is usually a different fibre from the garment and shrinks at its own rate, so a repair is a local stiffness anomaly that biases any nearby shrinkage or fray measurement. Recording it lets that region be excluded rather than silently averaged in.
- [ ] `BEFORE.ANOM.PAINT.R1.I01` (1/1, conditional, n_paint > 0)
      200 mm field centred on paint instance NN: the whole painted area if it fits,
      otherwise the most detailed 200 mm of it plus overlapping frames R1..Rn at >=30%
      overlap; every edge of the paint film, any existing cracking or flaking, >=40 mm of
      unpainted denim, and the nearest seam landmark.
      *why:* SEQUENCING CRITICAL: a painted print is what determines whether the garment can be machine-washed at all, and DENIM_0001 already took that branch. This frame must precede any wash decision, and it is the before-state of the component most likely to change visibly in the wash. Once washed, an uncracked before-state cannot be reconstructed.
- [ ] `BEFORE.ANOM.EMBROIDERY.R1.I01` (1/1, conditional, n_embroidery > 0)
      200 mm field centred on embroidery instance NN: the whole embroidered area,
      individual stitch penetrations resolvable at the densest point, the stabiliser/denim
      boundary, >=40 mm of plain denim around it, and the nearest seam landmark.
      *why:* Dense embroidery locally stiffens and pre-shrinks the ground fabric, so it is a shrinkage anomaly with a sharp boundary; its threads are also a different fibre that can bleed. Without a before frame at stitch resolution, post-wash puckering around it reads as fabric distortion.
- [ ] `BEFORE.ANOM.LOGO.R1.I01` (1/1, conditional, n_logos > 0)
      200 mm field centred on logo instance NN (woven tab, printed mark, stamped hardware
      logo): the whole logo with all text legible in the frame's own orientation, its
      attachment to the fabric, >=40 mm of surrounding denim, and the nearest seam
      landmark.
      *why:* Logos are the identity evidence that lets this exact garment be re-identified later, which is what the DATA_ELIGIBILITY exact_garment tri-state demands a written basis for; a verification nobody wrote down is not a verification. They are also small printed or woven elements that visibly degrade in a wash.
- [ ] `BEFORE.ANOM.PATCH.R1.I01` (1/1, conditional, n_patches > 0)
      200 mm field centred on applied-patch instance NN: the whole patch, its full
      attachment perimeter (stitched, fused or riveted), any lifting at the edges, >=40 mm
      of surrounding denim, and the nearest seam landmark.
      *why:* An applied patch is a second fabric with its own shrinkage rate bonded to the garment, and edge lifting is the most common wash failure; a fused patch can also release entirely. Its before-state perimeter is the only reference for judging that.
- [ ] `BEFORE.ANOM.STAIN.R1.I01` (1/1, conditional, n_stains > 0)
      200 mm field centred on stain instance NN: the whole stain including its diffuse
      boundary, >=40 mm of clean denim beyond the outermost visible edge, and the nearest
      seam landmark. Rig's standard two diffuse sources only -- no raking light, which
      invents stain edges.
      *why:* A stain is the one anomaly expected to shrink or vanish in the wash, so it is a positive control on whether the wash did anything at all, and its before-state extent is the measurand. An unrecorded stain that partially lifts reads afterwards as a new shade gradient.
- [ ] `BEFORE.ANOM.UNUSUAL_SEAM.I01.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_unusual_seams)
      200 mm field centred on unusual-seam instance NN (extra panel seam, non-standard
      felling, decorative seam, factory join): >=80 mm of the seam run, every topstitch
      row, both ends or a clear continuation off two frame edges, and >=40 mm of denim
      each side.
      *why:* A seam the standard region list does not name is a ply discontinuity the cut planner does not know about, and the frozen cut line may cross it. If the shears meet an unrecorded seam the cut is neither clean nor reproducible, and the fray measurement at that position is on a different structure from everywhere else on the loop.
- [ ] `BEFORE.ANOM.PREV_ALTERATION.I01.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_previous_alteration)
      200 mm field centred on alteration instance NN (re-hem, taper, shortened leg,
      replaced hardware): the alteration stitch line, the ORIGINAL stitch holes or crease
      if still visible, >=40 mm of denim each side, and the nearest original seam for
      reference.
      *why:* A previous alteration means the garment's recorded dimensions are not its factory dimensions, and a previously re-hemmed leg has fabric that has already been through a hem's stress and possibly a wash. It invalidates the inseam-derived positions this whole catalogue uses, so it must be found and recorded before those positions are trusted.

### Before cut — either face, lay 1, mount_overhead_fov350, main lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.OUTSEAM_L_UPPER.R1` (1/1, required)
      350 mm field, frame long axis ALONG the outseam, covering the outseam from the
      waistband corner downward: waistband lower seam in the top 10%, >=300 mm of
      continuous outseam down the frame centre, both felled-seam topstitch rows
      resolvable, >=50 mm of denim inboard and >=30 mm of backdrop outboard.
      *why:* The outseam is the leg's longest rigid reference line and the flat-lay's outer fold, so its straightness is the direct measure of how truly the leg was laid; its topstitch rows are also the seam most likely to pucker after a wash. Without a resolved seam run, post-wash leg-width change cannot be separated from a bowed lay.
- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.OUTSEAM_L_LOWER.R1` (1/1, required)
      350 mm field, long axis along the outseam, covering the LAST 350 mm of outseam above
      the hem: the hem seam in the bottom 10%, >=300 mm of continuous outseam up the frame
      centre, both topstitch rows resolvable, >=50 mm of denim inboard.
      *why:* Lower outseam is the offcut's structural spine and the segment that terminates at the factory hem, giving the finished-hem control against which the cut edge's fray is later judged. It cannot be retaken once the leg is separated and washed.
- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.INSEAM_L_UPPER.R1` (1/1, required)
      Legs spread per the lay protocol so the inseam is a free edge. 350 mm field, long
      axis along the left inseam from the crotch junction downward: crotch junction in the
      top 10%, >=300 mm of continuous inseam down the frame centre, the felled-seam
      topstitch row resolvable, >=50 mm of denim inboard.
      *why:* The inseam is the datum for the frozen cut definition (target inseam measured from the crotch seam along the inside leg), so its before-state geometry defines where the shears will go. If the inseam is not resolvable end-to-end before the cut, the cut length has no verifiable origin.
- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.INSEAM_L_LOWER.R1` (1/1, required)
      350 mm field along the left inseam covering the last 350 mm above the hem: hem seam
      in the bottom 10%, >=300 mm of continuous inseam, topstitch row resolvable, >=50 mm
      of denim inboard.
      *why:* Fixes the inseam-seam origin from which PROTOCOL SS5 numbers every fray position on the left offcut loop. Without it, position 1 on the offcut is chosen by eye after the wash and the numbering is not reproducible.
- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.OUTSEAM_R_UPPER.R1` (1/1, required)
      Mirror of OUTSEAM_L_UPPER: 350 mm field along the right outseam from the waistband
      corner down, >=300 mm of continuous seam, both topstitch rows resolvable.
      *why:* Right upper outseam; the L/R upper pair is what makes the cut's symmetry checkable against the garment's own construction rather than against an assumption that the two legs were identical to begin with.
- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.OUTSEAM_R_LOWER.R1` (1/1, required)
      Mirror of OUTSEAM_L_LOWER: 350 mm field covering the last 350 mm of right outseam
      above the hem, hem seam in the bottom 10%, >=300 mm of continuous seam.
      *why:* Right offcut's seam baseline; SS7 assigns the two offcuts to different wash conditions, so each needs its own before-wash seam record or the two arms are not comparable.
- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.INSEAM_R_UPPER.R1` (1/1, required)
      Mirror of INSEAM_L_UPPER: legs spread, 350 mm field along the right inseam from the
      crotch down, >=300 mm of continuous inseam, topstitch row resolvable.
      *why:* Right inseam datum for the cut. The frozen cut is perpendicular to the leg's midline, not square to the inseam, so both inseams must be resolved before the outseam offset can be computed for either leg.
- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.INSEAM_R_LOWER.R1` (1/1, required)
      Mirror of INSEAM_L_LOWER: 350 mm field along the right inseam covering the last 350
      mm above the hem, hem seam in the bottom 10%, >=300 mm of continuous inseam.
      *why:* Fixes the SS5 position-1 origin on the right offcut loop, and completes the four inseam/outseam segment set that lets the two offcuts be treated as independently measured samples.
- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.CUFF_STATE.R1` (1/2, conditional, has_cuffs)
      350 mm field horizontally across the left leg opening. R1 = the turn-up exactly AS
      RECEIVED, untouched. R2 = the identical framing after the turn-up has been unfolded
      and smoothed, with the fold crease visible. Both frames carry the whole leg opening
      plus >=60 mm of leg above the cuff.
      *why:* CONTRIBUTING_PAIRS is explicit that a cuffed or hemmed edge cannot fray however it is washed, so whether the garment arrived cuffed changes what the original inseam even means and where the crease has already set the fabric. Recording only the as-received state loses the true leg length; recording only the unfolded state destroys the evidence of how it was worn.
- [ ] `BEFORE.ANOM.PRINT_FADE.R1.I01` (1/1, conditional, n_printed_fade > 0)
      350 mm field centred on fade instance NN (whiskering fan, knee fade, honeycomb): the
      WHOLE fade pattern including its outer boundary where it returns to full-shade
      denim, plus the nearest seam so the pattern is relocatable. A 200 mm field is too
      small for a whisker fan, which is why this ANOM type uses the region tier.
      *why:* Fades are pre-existing shade gradients that a wash redistributes, so they are the strongest confound for any post-wash colour or shade measurement, and their boundaries are also convenient non-seam landmarks. Recorded only at whole-garment scale their boundaries are unresolvable; unrecorded, post-wash shade change is unattributable.
- [ ] `BEFORE.ANOM.ASYMMETRY.I01.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_asymmetry)
      350 mm field framed so that BOTH sides of the asymmetric feature pair are inside one
      frame with the garment's centre line at frame centre (e.g. both back pockets, both
      belt loop groups, both knee fades). If the pair cannot fit at 350 mm, shoot the two
      members as .I01 and .I02 at identical framing and say so in the manifest.
      *why:* Construction asymmetry recorded BEFORE the cut is what stops a post-wash L/R difference being read as differential shrinkage or an uneven cut. Capturing both members in one frame with one board makes the comparison immune to the scale and tilt differences that two separate frames would introduce.

### Before cut — either face, lay 2, mount_overhead_fov350, main lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.CUFF_STATE.R1` (2/2, conditional, has_cuffs)  **LIFT AND RE-LAY FIRST**
      350 mm field horizontally across the left leg opening. R1 = the turn-up exactly AS
      RECEIVED, untouched. R2 = the identical framing after the turn-up has been unfolded
      and smoothed, with the fold crease visible. Both frames carry the whole leg opening
      plus >=60 mm of leg above the cuff.
      *why:* CONTRIBUTING_PAIRS is explicit that a cuffed or hemmed edge cannot fray however it is washed, so whether the garment arrived cuffed changes what the original inseam even means and where the crease has already set the fabric. Recording only the as-received state loses the true leg length; recording only the unfolded state destroys the evidence of how it was worn.

### Before cut — BACK up, lay 1, mount_low_macro, tele lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.CONSTRUCTION.MACRO` (1/1, required)
      Turn the left leg inside out (or fold the hem back on itself and hold it flat with a
      weight placed away from the edge, never a pin) and fill the frame with about 100 mm
      of the hem allowance seen from the inside: the raw or overlocked cut edge of the
      allowance, the fold line or lines, every row of stitching, and the thread. Loop tape
      flat in frame 10 mm from the allowance edge. Optical axis perpendicular to the
      fabric plane.
      *why:* Hem construction determines whether the original hem is a valid finished-edge negative control at all. A single-fold overlocked hem, a double-fold lockstitch hem and a bound hem behave differently in the wash, and a chainstitched hem ropes. Without this frame the negative control is an untyped object and the post-wash comparison against the cut edge has no stated contrast.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.RIGHT.CONSTRUCTION.MACRO` (1/1, required)
      As BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.CONSTRUCTION.MACRO but for the right leg.
      *why:* Per-leg hem construction record, for the same reason as the left leg.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.PREVIOUS_ALTERATION.MACRO` (1/1, conditional, has_previous_alteration)
      PARAMETERISED OVER LEG. Leg inside out or hem folded back, frame about 100 mm of hem
      allowance centred on the evidence of alteration: a second stitch line, a shortened
      allowance, a different thread colour or gauge, a residual original crease line, a
      cut-and-rehemmed raw edge. Loop tape in frame with the alteration's loop coordinate
      legible.
      *why:* A previously shortened leg has a different fabric history at the hem: the surviving allowance may be shallower, the thread different, and the original crease still present. That history is a confound for the finished-hem control and for the garment's original_inseam_cm, and it is unrecoverable once the hem is cut off.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.RIGHT.PREVIOUS_ALTERATION.MACRO` (1/1, conditional, has_previous_alteration)
      PARAMETERISED OVER LEG. Leg inside out or hem folded back, frame about 100 mm of hem
      allowance centred on the evidence of alteration: a second stitch line, a shortened
      allowance, a different thread colour or gauge, a residual original crease line, a
      cut-and-rehemmed raw edge. Loop tape in frame with the alteration's loop coordinate
      legible.
      *why:* A previously shortened leg has a different fabric history at the hem: the surviving allowance may be shallower, the thread different, and the original crease still present. That history is a confound for the finished-hem control and for the garment's original_inseam_cm, and it is unrecoverable once the hem is cut off.

### Before cut — BACK up, lay 1, mount_macro_fov120, macro lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.POCKET.STITCHING_BACK_L.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_left_back_pocket)
      120 mm field on the busiest 120 mm of the left back pocket's decorative/arcuate
      stitching, including at least one top corner bar-tack. Individual stitch
      penetrations must be countable and the thread's ply visible; the pocket hem seam
      should cross one frame edge for location.
      *why:* Stitch pitch and thread condition are the only before/after evidence of thread shrinkage and seam pucker, and thread shrinks at a different rate from the fabric it is sewn into. At the 350 mm pocket framing the stitch line reads as a line, not as stitches, so pitch cannot be counted at all.
- [ ] `BEFORE.POCKET.STITCHING_BACK_R.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_right_back_pocket)
      Mirror of STITCHING_BACK_L: 120 mm field on the right back pocket's decorative
      stitching including at least one top corner bar-tack, stitch penetrations countable.
      *why:* Right-hand counterpart; stitch pitch differences between the two pockets before the wash are the control against which post-wash pucker asymmetry is judged.

### Before cut — BACK up, lay 1, mount_macro_fov150_tex, macro lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.TEX.BACK_L_MID.R1` (1/1, optional)
      150 mm field, garment back-up, on the left back leg at the 381 mm knee position,
      midway between inseam and outseam, containing a >=100 x 100 mm clean weave patch
      with no print, seam or hardware inside it.
      *why:* Back-face weave at the same height as the front reference, which is where a warp/weft face difference or a print-side finish difference would show. Marked optional because a heavily printed back panel can make it physically impossible; the point of declaring it is that its absence has to be recorded as an absence rather than passing unnoticed.

### Before cut — BACK up, lay 1, mount_macro_fov200, main lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.WAIST.BRAND_PATCH.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_brand_patch)
      200 mm field: the whole patch plus its full stitch perimeter and >=40 mm of
      surrounding denim/waistband. Patch flat and uncurled (do not flatten a permanently
      curled patch -- shoot it as it lies and say so). All printed or embossed text
      legible in the frame's own orientation.
      *why:* A leather or jacron patch is the strongest single-garment identity evidence, it deforms and darkens more than any other component in a wash, and its printed size/lot text is the only independent cross-check on the record's brand_optional and style fields (DENIM_0001 carries style_sku_unknown as a quality flag). Skipping it leaves both identity and the most wash-reactive component unrecorded.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WAIST.CROTCH_SEAM_BACK.R1` (1/1, required)
      200 mm field, garment back-up, centred on the junction where the back rise seam
      meets the two inseams: >=70 mm of each inseam radiating down-left and down-right,
      >=60 mm of back rise seam above, all reinforcement stitch rows complete.
      *why:* The back crotch is the other end of the rise measurand and the junction that carries the most ply-count change in a wash. Without it the back rise has a start point that cannot be located to better than a few millimetres.
- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.INTERSECT_YOKE_OUTSEAM_L.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_yoke)
      200 mm field, garment back-up, on the point where the yoke seam meets the left
      outseam: >=80 mm of yoke seam running inboard, >=80 mm of outseam running down,
      every topstitch row and the bar-tack if present, >=30 mm of backdrop outboard.
      *why:* The yoke/outseam junction is where three seam directions and the most plies meet on the back panel, so it is the back's stiffest point and the anchor that fixes the yoke V against the leg. Without it the yoke angle measured at 550 mm has no resolved end-point.
- [ ] `BEFORE.SEAM.INTERSECT_YOKE_OUTSEAM_R.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_yoke)
      Mirror of INTERSECT_YOKE_OUTSEAM_L: 200 mm field on the right yoke/outseam junction,
      >=80 mm of each seam, all topstitch rows and the bar-tack if present.
      *why:* Right yoke junction; the pair fixes both ends of the yoke seam so the yoke V can be measured as an angle rather than traced as a curve, which is what makes it lay-invariant.

### Before cut — BACK up, lay 1, mount_mid_overhead_hem, main lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.BACK_COMPLETE.OVERHEAD` (1/1, required)
      Garment turned back-up, left leg laid straight and smoothed, same mount height and
      board corner as the front frame. Frame the complete back-panel hem edge from the
      outseam to the inseam seam, plus 120 mm of leg above the hem, board flat in frame,
      loop tape on the surface 10 mm outboard of the edge with its coordinate continuing
      from where the front pass ended.
      *why:* Completes the original hem loop. PROTOCOL section 5 numbers positions front panel first, then back panel, so the back-panel run is half the loop coordinate and cannot be inferred from the front frame.
- [ ] `BEFORE.HEM.RIGHT.BACK_COMPLETE.OVERHEAD` (1/1, required)
      As BEFORE.HEM.LEFT.BACK_COMPLETE.OVERHEAD but for the right leg, same mount height,
      board corner, tape offset, lens and crop.
      *why:* Completes the right leg's original hem loop, for the same reason as the left.

### Before cut — BACK up, lay 1, mount_overhead_fov350, main lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.POCKET.BACK_L.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_left_back_pocket)
      350 mm field square-on to the left back pocket: all four corners plus >=50 mm of
      denim beyond each, the pocket hem seam across the top, any arcuate stitching
      complete and unclipped, both top corner bar-tacks or rivets inside.
      *why:* A back pocket is a rigid quadrilateral sewn onto a free panel: its four corners give a homography onto the back panel that no other feature provides, and its outline is the highest-contrast shape available for before/after registration of the back.
- [ ] `BEFORE.POCKET.BACK_R.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_right_back_pocket)
      Mirror of BACK_L: 350 mm field square-on to the right back pocket, all four corners
      with >=50 mm beyond each, hem seam, arcuate stitching complete, both top bar-
      tacks/rivets inside.
      *why:* Right-hand counterpart; the pair of pocket quadrilaterals is the back panel's only two-point rigid frame, and their relative placement is the primary evidence for has_asymmetry.

### Before cut — BACK up, lay 1, mount_overhead_fov550, main lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.WAIST.WAISTBAND_BACK.R1` (1/2, required)
      Garment back-up. 550 mm field, long axis horizontal. Whole waistband strip with both
      side-seam ends >=30 mm inside the frame edges, the centre-back seam at frame centre,
      and 40 mm of yoke below the waistband seam.
      *why:* Back waistband carries the centre-back seam and the brand patch seating, and is the back-face half of the registration anchor. Losing it means the post-wash back panel cannot be registered to the before state independently of the front.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WAIST.WAISTBAND_BACK.R1` (2/2, required)  **TAKE THE PHONE OFF THE MOUNT AND REMOUNT IT**
      Garment back-up. 550 mm field, long axis horizontal. Whole waistband strip with both
      side-seam ends >=30 mm inside the frame edges, the centre-back seam at frame centre,
      and 40 mm of yoke below the waistband seam.
      *why:* Back waistband carries the centre-back seam and the brand patch seating, and is the back-face half of the registration anchor. Losing it means the post-wash back panel cannot be registered to the before state independently of the front.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WAIST.BELT_LOOPS_BACK.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_back_belt_loops)
      550 mm field on the back waistband: every back and side-back belt loop with both
      bar-tacks visible, loops unfolded, 40 mm of waistband above and 40 mm of yoke below.
      *why:* Back loop spacing is the along-waist shrinkage ruler for the back panel, and the centre-back loop marks the centre-back seam without a mark being drawn on the garment. Without it the back waistband has no interior landmarks at all.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WAIST.RISE_BACK.R1` (1/1, required)
      550 mm field, long axis VERTICAL, garment back-up: top of the waistband in the top
      10%, the back crotch-seam junction >=60 mm above the frame bottom, the yoke seam and
      both back pockets' inner edges inside.
      *why:* Carries the whole back_rise_cm measurand in one image. DENIM_0001 has back_rise_cm null, so without this frame a required schema dimension stays unmeasurable forever once the garment is cut.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WAIST.YOKE_BACK.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_yoke)
      550 mm field, garment back-up: the whole yoke seam as a shallow V from left outseam
      to right outseam, waistband lower seam in the top 20%, >=80 mm of back leg panel
      below the yoke's lowest point, both yoke/outseam junctions >=30 mm inside the frame
      edges.
      *why:* The yoke is a rigid triangulated seam that fixes the back panel's shape independently of how the legs were laid, so its V angle is the least lay-sensitive back-panel geometry the garment has. Without it, post-wash back-panel distortion cannot be separated from re-lay differences.
- [ ] `BEFORE.LEG.THIGH_BACK_L.R1` (1/1, required)
      550 mm field, garment back-up, long axis vertical along the left leg: back crotch
      junction in the top 10%, frame bottom >=80 mm below the 381 mm knee position, both
      seams inside with >=40 mm of backdrop beyond the outseam.
      *why:* Back thigh is the retained back panel and, on this pilot garment, the carrier of the painted print that determines the wash branch. Without it the retained back panel has no before-state at panel scale.
- [ ] `BEFORE.LEG.THIGH_BACK_R.R1` (1/1, required)
      Mirror of THIGH_BACK_L on the right leg: 550 mm field, back crotch junction in the
      top 10%, frame bottom >=80 mm below the 381 mm knee position.
      *why:* Right-hand retained back panel; completes the four-panel before-state of everything the garment keeps after the cut.

### Before cut — BACK up, lay 1, mount_overhead_locked, main lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.WHOLE.B00.R1` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 B00. Flip the garment about its LONG axis so the waistband stays at the
      top of frame and the garment's left leg moves to the image LEFT. Back up, legs to
      the frozen gap marks, smoothed by hand, no pins, whole garment clear of every frame
      edge, board in its frozen corner. Camera untouched.
      *why:* The back silhouette, needed because the cut line is defined on the leg's centre line — the midline between inseam and outseam — and a front-only view cannot establish where the outseam runs on the back panel. Rep 1 of the back relay-only arm.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WHOLE.B00.R2` (1/1, required)
      Identical to BEFORE.WHOLE.B00.R1 after a complete lift and re-lay. Camera, exposure
      and white balance untouched.
      *why:* Rep 2 of the back relay-only arm. Two relay-only back frames plus one repositioned one is the smallest allocation that lets the back series carry one of each kind, which is what is needed to test whether the front series' variance components are front-specific rather than to re-estimate them from scratch.
- [ ] `BEFORE.WHOLE.B00.R3` (1/1, required)
      As BEFORE.WHOLE.B00.R1 but reached by dismounting the phone, re-laying the garment
      from scratch, remounting, and re-establishing framing and locks.
      *why:* The back series' single repositioned capture. The back panel is flatter and less structured than the front — no fly, no front pockets standing proud — so it responds differently to re-laying, and a reposition sample here is what shows whether the front's relay-versus-reposition split generalises or is an artefact of the front panel's structure.

### Before cut — BACK up, lay 1, oblique_station_30deg, main lens

- [ ] `BEFORE.OBLIQUE.BL1` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 BL1. Garment in the B00 back-up lay (flipped about its long axis,
      waistband still at the top, garment-left leg now on the image LEFT). Stand at the
      taped BACK-LEFT station, on the garment's left side. Optical axis about 30 degrees
      from the surface normal, tilted across the leg toward your station, aimed at the
      centre of leg section 1 (0.125 of the inseam below the crotch seam). Leg cross-width
      fills the guide; both leg edges plus 50 mm of backdrop beyond each in frame; board
      in frame beside the section.
      *why:* The back thigh at raking light, above the cut line. The back panel carries the yoke and the back pockets and is where the leg's outseam is easiest to trace, so the back obliques are the ones that establish where the leg's centre line — the datum PROTOCOL §3.1's frozen cut is perpendicular to — actually runs.
- [ ] `BEFORE.OBLIQUE.BL2` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 BL2. As BL1 from the BACK-LEFT station, aimed at the centre of leg
      section 2 (0.375 of the inseam below the crotch seam).
      *why:* The back face of the cut region. The cut is a single line through both fabric layers, so the back panel's fabric at the cut is as much a subject of the fray measurement as the front's, and PROTOCOL §5 numbers fray positions around the whole hem LOOP — front panel then back panel. This is the back panel's before state for that loop.
- [ ] `BEFORE.OBLIQUE.BL3` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 BL3. As BL1 from the BACK-LEFT station, aimed at the centre of leg
      section 3 (0.625 of the inseam below the crotch seam).
      *why:* The left offcut's back face at the knee. Because §5 measures fray around the offcut's whole raw-edge loop as well as the garment's, the offcut's back panel is a measured surface too and needs a before-cut record at the same raking light as everything it will be compared with.
- [ ] `BEFORE.OBLIQUE.BL4` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 BL4. As BL1 from the BACK-LEFT station, aimed at the centre of leg
      section 4 (0.875 of the inseam below the crotch seam), with the original hem edge
      and 50 mm of backdrop below it in frame.
      *why:* Completes the left back leg. The back of the original hem is where hem curl is most often visible, and PROTOCOL §5's edge-curl measurand is defined on the garment laid front-up after conditioning — so a back-face record of the hem before anything happens is the only pre-state for a curl that may already exist on this side.
- [ ] `BEFORE.OBLIQUE.BR1` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 BR1. Garment in the B00 back-up lay. Stand at the taped BACK-RIGHT
      station, on the garment's right side (image RIGHT in the back-up lay). Optical axis
      about 30 degrees from the surface normal, tilted across the leg toward your station,
      aimed at the centre of leg section 1 (0.125 of the inseam below the crotch seam).
      Leg cross-width fills the guide; both leg edges plus 50 mm of backdrop in frame;
      board in frame beside the section.
      *why:* The right back thigh above the cut line, completing the four-quadrant coverage at section 1. With FL1, FR1 and BL1 this gives the topmost leg section from all four stations, which is the only section photographed from every direction and therefore the one where a surface feature can be confirmed as real rather than a lighting artefact of one station.
- [ ] `BEFORE.OBLIQUE.BR2` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 BR2. As BR1 from the BACK-RIGHT station, aimed at the centre of leg
      section 2 (0.375 of the inseam below the crotch seam).
      *why:* The back face of the right leg's cut region, the fourth and last view of the fabric the cut line will pass through. All four cut-region obliques (FL2, FR2, BL2, BR2) together are the complete before-state surface record of the material that becomes the raw edge whose fraying this entire project exists to predict.
- [ ] `BEFORE.OBLIQUE.BR3` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 BR3. As BR1 from the BACK-RIGHT station, aimed at the centre of leg
      section 3 (0.625 of the inseam below the crotch seam).
      *why:* The right offcut's back face at the knee. PROTOCOL §6 allows the offcuts to serve as the repeat-wash noise-floor samples, which makes their before state part of a repeatability measurement rather than a description — and a noise floor computed against a missing baseline is not a noise floor.
- [ ] `BEFORE.OBLIQUE.BR4` (1/1, required)
      PROTOCOL §2 BR4. As BR1 from the BACK-RIGHT station, aimed at the centre of leg
      section 4 (0.875 of the inseam below the crotch seam), with the original hem edge
      and 50 mm of backdrop below it in frame. This is the sixteenth and last oblique of
      the before state.
      *why:* Completes the systematic 4-quadrant x 4-section grid, so every band of both legs is recorded from both a front and a back station under raking light. The grid's value is its completeness: an incomplete grid cannot support the claim that a post-wash surface change is localised, because a region with no before-state oblique cannot be shown to have changed or to have stayed the same.

### Marked for cutting — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_low_macro, macro lens

- [ ] `MARKED.CUT.LEFT.MARK_MACRO` (1/1, required)
      Left leg. Fill the frame with the marked line where it crosses the INSEAM, with the
      tape still in place showing the distance from the crotch seam. Rule flat in the
      garment's plane.
      *why:* The physical mark's position on the inseam is the number the second person verifies and the one the prediction is scored against.
- [ ] `MARKED.CUT.RIGHT.MARK_MACRO` (1/1, required)
      Right leg, same frame as the left. Marked line crossing the INSEAM with the tape in
      place.
      *why:* The right leg is marked separately and can be marked wrongly separately; one frame per leg is what makes that visible.

### Marked for cutting — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_overhead, main lens

- [ ] `MARKED.CUT.ANGLE_LEFT` (1/1, required)
      Left leg, straightedge laid on both marks. Frame the full width of the leg so the
      whole marked line is visible from inseam to outseam, with the board in frame for
      scale.
      *why:* The angle of the marked line is what the prediction predicts; measuring it needs both ends of the line in one frame at a known scale.
- [ ] `MARKED.MEASURE.LEFT.INSEAM_TAPE` (1/1, required)
      Left leg flat and straight. Tape running along the INSEAM from the crotch seam to
      the mark, zero at the crotch seam, the reading at the mark legible without zooming.
      *why:* A photograph of the tape in place is the only evidence that the marked distance is the distance that was intended; a number typed into a form is not.
- [ ] `MARKED.MEASURE.LEFT.OUTSEAM_TAPE` (1/1, required)
      Left leg. Tape along the OUTSEAM from the crotch-level seam to the mark. The reading
      must be the inseam target PLUS the digital outseam offset the cut packet prints.
      *why:* The cut is perpendicular to the leg's centre line, not square to the inseam, so the outseam mark is deliberately further down. This frame is what shows the offset was applied.
- [ ] `MARKED.CUT.ANGLE_RIGHT` (1/1, required)
      Right leg, straightedge on both marks, full leg width in frame.
      *why:* As for the left leg, measured separately.
- [ ] `MARKED.MEASURE.RIGHT.INSEAM_TAPE` (1/1, required)
      Right leg, tape along the INSEAM from the crotch seam to the mark.
      *why:* Per-leg evidence: the two legs are marked independently and must be verified independently.
- [ ] `MARKED.MEASURE.RIGHT.OUTSEAM_TAPE` (1/1, required)
      Right leg, tape along the OUTSEAM to the mark, including the offset.
      *why:* Per-leg evidence that the offset was applied on this leg too.
- [ ] `MARKED.PREDICTION.OVERLAY_COMPARISON` (1/1, required)
      Print or display the cut overlay the tool generated and photograph it beside the
      marked garment, or photograph the marked garment and hold the printed overlay in the
      same frame. Both the physical mark and the predicted line must be visible together.
      *why:* The comparison between the physical mark and the digital prediction is a claim about the prediction, and it needs a frame in which both appear -- not two frames taken apart.
- [ ] `MARKED.WHOLE.FRONT_OVERHEAD` (1/1, required)
      Garment front-up, marked, laid exactly as for the before-state overheads: waistband
      at the top, legs parallel at the frozen gap, board flat in its usual corner. BOTH
      cut marks and both straightedge lines must be legible in the frame.
      *why:* The whole-garment record of where the cut was actually marked, in the same framing as the before-state overhead so the marked line can be registered against the predicted one.

### Immediately after cutting — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_low_macro, tele lens

- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.HEM.LEFT.MACRO.P01` (1/1, required)
      PARAMETERISED SERIES, identical geometry to POSTWASH.HEM.LEFT.MACRO.Pnn and shot at
      the same station with the same lens, working distance and tape offset. For each
      macro centre index c: about 100 mm of the freshly cut RAW edge centred on loop
      position Pc, optical axis perpendicular to the fabric plane, certified loop tape
      flat on the surface 10 mm outboard of the edge, zero at the inseam seam, with the
      graduations for Pc-2, Pc and Pc+2 all legible and all at least 10 mm inside the
      frame edge. Front-panel positions front-up, back-panel positions with the leg
      turned, coordinate continuing. Handle the cut edge as little as possible: an
      unwashed raw edge sheds threads on contact and every thread lost here is a thread
      the post-wash comparison never sees.  [frame 1 of 6 around the loop: arc 0-76 mm
      from the inseam seam, covering measurement position(s) 1, 2, 3, 4]
      *why:* Fray is a CHANGE, and a post-wash loop map on its own cannot express one. This is the unwashed state of the same physical edge at the same positions and the same scale, so every post-wash position has a matched zero. It also captures the shear's own edge signature - a single continuous stroke and a stepped stroke leave different edges - which is the largest non-wash source of variation around the loop. Ownership note: this series mirrors part (b) into the immediate_after state and may overlap another agent's scope; if so, keep this geometry and drop the duplicate.
