### Immediately after cutting — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_low_macro, macro lens

- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.HEM.LEFT.INSEAM_JUNCTION` (1/1, required)
      Fill the frame with the point where the new raw edge meets the INSEAM seam, rule in
      the garment's plane touching the edge.
      *why:* The seam junctions are where the cut crosses a thick seam, and they fray unlike the open weave either side of them.
- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.HEM.LEFT.OUTSEAM_JUNCTION` (1/1, required)
      The point where the new raw edge meets the OUTSEAM seam, rule in plane.
      *why:* The outseam is often selvedge or a felled seam and is the thickest crossing on the loop.
- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.IRREGULARITY.LEFT.INN.I01` (1/1, conditional, n_cut_irregularities > 0)
      One frame per cutting irregularity on this leg -- a step, a stray snip, a wobble --
      filled by the irregularity with the rule beside it.
      *why:* An irregularity is a local departure the fray model will otherwise attribute to the fabric.
- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.HEM.RIGHT.INSEAM_JUNCTION` (1/1, required)
      Fill the frame with the point where the new raw edge meets the INSEAM seam, rule in
      the garment's plane touching the edge.
      *why:* The seam junctions are where the cut crosses a thick seam, and they fray unlike the open weave either side of them.
- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.HEM.RIGHT.OUTSEAM_JUNCTION` (1/1, required)
      The point where the new raw edge meets the OUTSEAM seam, rule in plane.
      *why:* The outseam is often selvedge or a felled seam and is the thickest crossing on the loop.
- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.IRREGULARITY.RIGHT.INN.I01` (1/1, conditional, n_cut_irregularities > 0)
      One frame per cutting irregularity on this leg -- a step, a stray snip, a wobble --
      filled by the irregularity with the rule beside it.
      *why:* An irregularity is a local departure the fray model will otherwise attribute to the fabric.

### Immediately after cutting — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_overhead, main lens

- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.CUT.LEFT.ACTUAL_INSEAM_TAPE` (1/1, required)
      Tape along the INSEAM from the crotch seam to the actual cut edge, reading legible.
      *why:* What was intended and what was cut are different numbers, and the second is the one the post-cut geometry must be scored against.
- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.CUT.LEFT.ACTUAL_OUTSEAM_TAPE` (1/1, required)
      Tape along the OUTSEAM from the crotch-level seam to the actual cut edge.
      *why:* With the inseam reading, this gives the cut's actual angle rather than its intended one.
- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.CUT.RIGHT.ACTUAL_INSEAM_TAPE` (1/1, required)
      Tape along the INSEAM from the crotch seam to the actual cut edge, reading legible.
      *why:* What was intended and what was cut are different numbers, and the second is the one the post-cut geometry must be scored against.
- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.CUT.RIGHT.ACTUAL_OUTSEAM_TAPE` (1/1, required)
      Tape along the OUTSEAM from the crotch-level seam to the actual cut edge.
      *why:* With the inseam reading, this gives the cut's actual angle rather than its intended one.
- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.RAW_EDGE.LEFT.FRONT_COMPLETE` (1/1, required)
      The complete raw cut edge of the left leg, front panel, from inseam seam to outseam
      seam, with 60 mm of leg above it and the board in frame. The edge must run end to
      end across the frame.
      *why:* The whole raw edge before washing is the baseline every fray measurement is a change from.
- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.RAW_EDGE.RIGHT.FRONT_COMPLETE` (1/1, required)
      The complete raw cut edge of the right leg, front panel, from inseam seam to outseam
      seam, with 60 mm of leg above it and the board in frame. The edge must run end to
      end across the frame.
      *why:* The whole raw edge before washing is the baseline every fray measurement is a change from.
- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.WHOLE.FRONT_OVERHEAD.R1` (1/1, required)
      Garment front-up after cutting, laid exactly as the before-state overheads:
      waistband at the top, both legs parallel at the frozen gap, not touching, board flat
      in its usual corner. The whole garment including both new hems must be inside the
      frame.
      *why:* Silhouette and scale immediately after the cut and before any wash, so shrinkage is measured against the cut garment rather than the uncut one.
- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.WHOLE.FRONT_OVERHEAD.R2` (1/1, required)
      Garment front-up after cutting, laid exactly as the before-state overheads:
      waistband at the top, both legs parallel at the frozen gap, not touching, board flat
      in its usual corner. The whole garment including both new hems must be inside the
      frame.
      *why:* Silhouette and scale immediately after the cut and before any wash, so shrinkage is measured against the cut garment rather than the uncut one.

### Immediately after cutting — BACK up, lay 1, mount_overhead, main lens

- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.RAW_EDGE.LEFT.BACK_COMPLETE` (1/1, required)
      The complete raw cut edge of the left leg, back panel, leg turned back-up, same
      framing.
      *why:* The back panel of the loop frays differently from the front; a front-only record is half the loop.
- [ ] `IMMEDIATE_AFTER.RAW_EDGE.RIGHT.BACK_COMPLETE` (1/1, required)
      The complete raw cut edge of the right leg, back panel, leg turned back-up, same

### Offcuts before wash — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_overhead, main lens

- [ ] `OFFCUT_BEFORE.LEFT.FACE_FRONT` (1/1, required)
      Offcut front-up, flat, whole sample in frame with the board, before washing.
      *why:* Dimensions and appearance of the sample as a whole, before washing.
- [ ] `OFFCUT_BEFORE.RIGHT.FACE_FRONT` (1/1, required)
      Offcut front-up, flat, whole sample in frame with the board, before washing.

      garment's, made by the same stroke of the same shears - laid flat, same station,
      lens, working distance, 10 mm tape offset, 100 mm framing and centre set as
      IMMEDIATE_AFTER.HEM.LEFT.MACRO.Pnn. Shot before washing.  [frame 1 of 6 around the
      loop: arc 0-76 mm from the inseam seam, covering measurement position(s) 1, 2, 3, 4]

### After washing — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_low_macro, tele lens

- [ ] `POSTWASH.HEM.LEFT.INSEAM_DATUM.MACRO.P01` (1/2, required)
      Fill the frame with about 100 mm of cut edge centred on the inseam seam, which is
      loop position P01 and the origin of the whole coordinate. The inseam seam must be
      visible running up from the edge, the tape's ZERO graduation must be legible and
      sitting on the seam, and the graduations for the next two positions in each
      direction (P02, P03 forward and the last two positions of the loop backward) must
      all be legible and at least 10 mm inside the frame edge.
      *why:* Proves the origin of the loop coordinate. Every position index in the map is defined as an arc distance from this seam, so if the origin is only asserted, the entire map's registration to the garment is unverifiable and the before/after position matching is meaningless. The duplicated capture also supplies the noise floor against which any measured fray difference between positions must be judged.

      PARAMETERISED SERIES - THE LOOP MAP. The generator emits one instance per macro
      centre index c, with Pnn replaced by that zero-padded index; the centre set is
      computed from the measured post-wash cut-edge circumference (see rationale). For
      each instance: fill the frame with about 100 mm of the raw cut edge centred on loop
      position Pc, optical axis perpendicular to the fabric plane, certified loop tape
      flat on the surface 10 mm outboard of the edge (never on the fabric and never
      touching the fringe), zero on the inseam seam, running toward the FRONT of the leg
      first. The graduations for Pc-2, Pc-1, Pc, Pc+1 and Pc+2 must all be legible and all
      at least 10 mm inside every frame edge, and the full fringe depth at every one of
      those positions must be inside the frame with at least 10 mm of backdrop beyond the
      longest thread. Positions from P01 to the outseam crossing are shot with the garment
      front-up; the remaining positions are shot with the leg turned back-up and the tape
      coordinate continuing without reset. Do not smooth, lift, blow on or otherwise touch
      the fringe anywhere in the series.  [frame 1 of 6 around the loop: arc 0-76 mm from
      the inseam seam, covering measurement position(s) 1, 2, 3, 4]
      *why:* This is the measurement. PROTOCOL section 5 requires fray depth and thread count at every 2 cm position around the closed cut-edge loop, and this overlapping series is what makes 'every position' provable rather than asserted: consecutive frames share at least one position, so the coverage of the loop can be checked frame to frame, and any gap is visible as a position no frame supports. Shot at 0.10 mm/px so a 0.5 mm fray depth is readable, which is the resolution EXP_0016 says the whole-garment route never reaches.

### After washing — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_macro_fov150_tex, macro lens

- [ ] `POSTWASH.TEX.FRONT_L_UPPER.R1` (1/1, required)
      150 mm field on the left front leg, 100 mm below the crotch junction, midway between
      inseam and outseam. The frame must contain a >=100 x 100 mm patch of continuous body
      weave with NO seam, hardware, print, fade edge or pocket bag inside it. Fabric flat
      and un-stretched; camera perpendicular to the fabric plane.  [Reproduce the framing
      of BEFORE.TEX.FRONT_L_UPPER.R1 exactly: the app shows it as a ghost overlay, which
      is a capture aid and never evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.TEX.FRONT_L_UPPER.R1. GATE_TEX derivation: a denim warp yarn is roughly 0.4-0.6 mm wide. Two pixels per yarn is only the Nyquist limit -- it detects the twill periodicity but cannot separate a yarn from its neighbour. Eight pixels across the NARROWEST yarn (0.4 mm) is what lets the twill diagonal be traced and a yarn width be measured, giving 0.4/8 = 0.05 mm/px as the ceiling. On a 4032 px long edge that is a 200 mm field; specifying 150 mm leaves margin and lands near 0.037 mm/px, about 11 px per 0.4 mm yarn. The 100 mm clean patch is exactly four ChArUco squares (25.0 mm, protocol/charuco_board.json), so it is directly comparable to a board-scaled measurement. Without this the post-wash weave comparison has no before-state at a scale where shrinkage-driven yarn crowding is visible at all.

### After washing — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_macro_fov200, main lens

- [ ] `POSTWASH.WAIST.CROTCH_SEAM_FRONT.R1` (1/1, required)
      200 mm field centred on the four-way junction where the fly bottom, the two front
      leg panels and the two inseams meet: >=70 mm of each inseam radiating down-left and
      down-right, the fly bottom bar-tack at the top, all crotch reinforcement stitch rows
      complete and unclipped.  [Reproduce the framing of BEFORE.WAIST.CROTCH_SEAM_FRONT.R1
      exactly: the app shows it as a ghost overlay, which is a capture aid and never
      evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.WAIST.CROTCH_SEAM_FRONT.R1. The front crotch is the origin of the inseam measurement and the single highest-ply junction on the garment, so it fixes where every inseam-referenced length starts and is where wash pucker appears first. At the 550 mm rise framing the junction is a few dozen pixels and the ply structure is unreadable.
- [ ] `POSTWASH.POCKET.COIN.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_coin_pocket)
      200 mm field: the whole coin/watch pocket including both upper corners, its full
      hem, every stitch row and any rivets, plus >=40 mm of the front pocket opening it
      sits inside so its position is recoverable.  [Reproduce the framing of
      BEFORE.POCKET.COIN.R1 exactly: the app shows it as a ghost overlay, which is a
      capture aid and never evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.POCKET.COIN.R1. The coin pocket is a small, sharply bounded, four-to-six-ply patch on an otherwise two-ply field, so it is the most sensitive local shrinkage witness on the garment. It is also the feature most often absent, which is why its shot is conditional rather than required.

### After washing — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_mid_overhead_hem, main lens

- [ ] `POSTWASH.HEM.LEFT.COMPLETE_OVERHEAD` (1/2, required)
      After the section 4 conditioning period and with the garment laid front-up and
      untouched since it was laid. Frame the complete front-panel run of the left leg's
      cut edge from inseam seam to outseam, plus 120 mm of leg above it, plus the ChArUco
      board flat in the usual corner of the frame, plus the certified loop tape on the
      surface 10 mm outboard of the edge with its zero on the inseam seam. The cut edge
      must run end to end across the frame with at least 20 mm of backdrop beyond both
      ends. Do not smooth, flatten or press the fringe.
      *why:* The only post-wash frame in which a ChArUco board and the loop tape appear together, so it is the sole machine-checkable link between the board's mm/px and every macro's human-read scale. It also supplies the post-wash cut-edge circumference that the position count is derived from, and it gives hem_roughness a whole-edge frame at native resolution.
- [ ] `POSTWASH.HEM.LEFT.COMPLETE_OVERHEAD` (2/2, required)  **TAKE THE PHONE OFF THE MOUNT AND REMOUNT IT**
      After the section 4 conditioning period and with the garment laid front-up and
      untouched since it was laid. Frame the complete front-panel run of the left leg's
      cut edge from inseam seam to outseam, plus 120 mm of leg above it, plus the ChArUco
      board flat in the usual corner of the frame, plus the certified loop tape on the
      surface 10 mm outboard of the edge with its zero on the inseam seam. The cut edge
      must run end to end across the frame with at least 20 mm of backdrop beyond both
      ends. Do not smooth, flatten or press the fringe.
      *why:* The only post-wash frame in which a ChArUco board and the loop tape appear together, so it is the sole machine-checkable link between the board's mm/px and every macro's human-read scale. It also supplies the post-wash cut-edge circumference that the position count is derived from, and it gives hem_roughness a whole-edge frame at native resolution.

      *why:* Post-wash metric anchor and circumference source for the right leg.
- [ ] `POSTWASH.HEM.RIGHT.COMPLETE_OVERHEAD` (2/2, required)  **TAKE THE PHONE OFF THE MOUNT AND REMOUNT IT**
      As POSTWASH.HEM.LEFT.COMPLETE_OVERHEAD but for the right leg, same mount height,

### After washing — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_overhead, main lens

- [ ] `POSTWASH.COLOUR.REFERENCE` (1/1, required)
      Grey/white reference card laid on the garment's upper thigh, both card and fabric
      filling a third of the frame each, exposure and white balance locked to the
      session's frozen values.
      *why:* Colour change through washing is only readable against a reference in the same frame under the same exposure; a remembered white balance is not a reference.
- [ ] `POSTWASH.WHOLE.F00.R1` (1/1, required)
      Garment front-up after washing and conditioning, laid exactly as the before-state
      overheads: waistband at the top, legs parallel at the frozen gap, never touching,
      board flat in its usual corner, whole garment in frame.
      *why:* Five independent re-lays after washing measure the same lay-to-lay variance as before it, so a shrinkage difference can be told from a laying difference.

### After washing — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_overhead_fov350, main lens

- [ ] `POSTWASH.POCKET.FRONT_OPENING_L.R1` (1/1, required)
      350 mm field with the whole pocket opening curve running corner-to-corner across the
      frame from the waistband seam to the side seam; both terminal rivets or bar-tacks
      inside with >=40 mm of denim beyond each; the pocket bag edge included if it shows
      through.  [Reproduce the framing of BEFORE.POCKET.FRONT_OPENING_L.R1 exactly: the
      app shows it as a ghost overlay, which is a capture aid and never evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.POCKET.FRONT_OPENING_L.R1. The front pocket opening is a curve of known construction whose two ends are rivets -- a rigid two-point span plus a shape. It is also the boundary of a double-ply region that shrinks differently from the single-ply panel beside it, which is the mechanism behind post-wash front-panel pucker.
- [ ] `POSTWASH.POCKET.FRONT_OPENING_R.R1` (1/1, required)
      Mirror of FRONT_OPENING_L: 350 mm field, whole right pocket opening curve corner-to-
      corner, both terminal rivets/bar-tacks with >=40 mm of denim beyond each.
      [Reproduce the framing of BEFORE.POCKET.FRONT_OPENING_R.R1 exactly: the app shows it
      as a ghost overlay, which is a capture aid and never evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.POCKET.FRONT_OPENING_R.R1. Right-hand counterpart, and half of the only L/R symmetry evidence on the front panel; the coin pocket sits inside one of the two and biases its ply count.

### After washing — FRONT up, lay 1, mount_overhead_fov550, main lens

- [ ] `POSTWASH.WAIST.WAISTBAND_FRONT.R1` (1/2, required)
      Garment front-up. 550 mm field, long axis horizontal. Whole waistband as a strip:
      top edge at 15% down the frame, strip bottom 40 mm below the waistband's lower seam
      so pocket-top and fly-top junctions are inside; both side-seam ends >=30 mm inside
      the left/right frame edges.  [Reproduce the framing of
      BEFORE.WAIST.WAISTBAND_FRONT.R1 exactly: the app shows it as a ghost overlay, which
      is a capture aid and never evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.WAIST.WAISTBAND_FRONT.R1. The waistband is the only landmark that survives the cut unchanged, so it is the before/after registration anchor and the shrinkage measurand. Two repetitions with a FULL RE-LAY are the only honest re-lay noise floor for this framing; EXP_0021 warns that simulated re-captures cannot move the fabric and therefore bound error from above only. Without it every later before/after delta silently carries lay variance.
- [ ] `POSTWASH.WAIST.BELT_LOOPS_FRONT.R1` (1/1, conditional, has_belt_loops)
      550 mm field on the front waistband: every front and side-front belt loop inside
      with BOTH its top and bottom bar-tacks visible, 40 mm of waistband above and below,
      loops lying flat and unfolded (unfold by hand before shooting).  [Reproduce the
      framing of BEFORE.WAIST.BELT_LOOPS_FRONT.R1 exactly: the app shows it as a ghost
      overlay, which is a capture aid and never evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.WAIST.BELT_LOOPS_FRONT.R1. Belt loops are discrete, evenly spaced, high-contrast fiducials along the waistband -- the best available landmark set for measuring differential shrinkage ALONG the waist rather than across it. Folded loops in the main waistband frame make those spacings unmeasurable.
- [ ] `POSTWASH.WAIST.RISE_FRONT.R1` (1/1, required)
      550 mm field, long axis VERTICAL: top of the waistband in the top 10% of the frame,
      the front crotch-seam junction >=60 mm above the frame bottom, full fly width plus
      the inner edge of both front pocket openings.  [Reproduce the framing of
      BEFORE.WAIST.RISE_FRONT.R1 exactly: the app shows it as a ghost overlay, which is a
      capture aid and never evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.WAIST.RISE_FRONT.R1. This frame must contain the entire front_rise_cm measurand (waistband top to crotch seam) in ONE image, so the rise can be re-measured from pixels after the wash without stitching two frames. PROTOCOL requires two readings per dimension; a rise split across frames cannot be re-derived at all.

### After washing — either face, lay 1, mount_grazing_table, tele lens

- [ ] `POSTWASH.HEM.LEFT.CURL_INSTANCE.INN.MACRO.I01` (1/1, conditional, n_curl_positions > 0)
      PARAMETERISED OVER LEG AND INSTANCE. One instance per visually conspicuous curl or
      wave in the cut edge, Inn replaced by the zero-padded 1-based instance index from
      the pilot ledger's instance table. Grazing station, axis in the surface plane and
      perpendicular to the local tangent, vertical steel rule at the frame centre, framed
      tight on the single feature with its loop coordinate readable from the tape and at
      least 20 mm of flatter edge visible on each side for reference.
      *why:* The regular curl series samples at the macro centres, so a single tall wave lying between two centres would be averaged away or missed. Since section 5 asks for the MAXIMUM vertical lift within +/-5 mm of each position, a conspicuous local maximum is exactly the value the protocol wants and exactly the value a regularly spaced series can drop.
- [ ] `POSTWASH.HEM.LEFT.SIDE_CURL.P01` (1/1, required)
      PARAMETERISED SERIES sharing the loop map's macro centres, restricted to centres
      whose supported positions lie on the FRONT panel. Garment laid front-up after the
      section 4 conditioning period and not touched since. Grazing station: optical axis
      in the surface plane, horizontal, perpendicular to the local cut-edge tangent at
      position Pc; plain dark card stood behind the leg; vertical steel rule stood on the
      surface at the frame centre with its zero touching the surface, just outside the
      fabric. Frame about 100 mm of edge in silhouette so positions Pc-2 .. Pc+2 are all
      inside it, with the surface line visible right across the frame. Do not re-lay,
      smooth, lift or press the garment anywhere in this series, and shoot the whole
      series in one uninterrupted session.  [frame 1 of 6 around the loop: arc 0-76 mm
      from the inseam seam, covering measurement position(s) 1, 2]
      *why:* Edge curl is the third PROTOCOL section 5 measurand and the only one that cannot be recovered from any overhead frame at any resolution. It is also the most perishable: section 5 defines it on the garment laid front-up after conditioning, so it exists only in that single untouched lay and is destroyed by the first re-lay, turn or press. If this series is not shot in the conditioning window, curl is UNAVAILABLE_CHECK for the whole garment and no later capture can substitute.

### After washing — either face, lay 1, mount_low_macro, tele lens

- [ ] `POSTWASH.HEM.LEFT.OUTSEAM_CROSSING.MACRO` (1/1, required)
      Fill the frame with about 100 mm of cut edge centred on the outseam, framed so that
      the front-panel run and the back-panel run of the loop are BOTH visible meeting at
      the outseam, with the tape graduation at the crossing legible and the graduations
      two positions either side of it legible and at least 10 mm inside the frame edge. If
      the two runs cannot be shown in one frame with the leg flat, shoot the leg opened
      out over a rounded former of known diameter and record the former's diameter in the
      ledger.
      *why:* Closes the loop. PROTOCOL section 5 numbers positions continuously from the inseam seam through the front panel and on through the back panel, which crosses the outseam once; that crossing is the single point where the index sequence could silently break, and it is also the point where the cut passes through a thick multi-layer seam and fray behaviour genuinely differs.
- [ ] `POSTWASH.HEM.RIGHT.OUTSEAM_CROSSING.MACRO` (1/1, required)
      As POSTWASH.HEM.LEFT.OUTSEAM_CROSSING.MACRO but for the right leg.
      *why:* Closes the right leg's loop.

### After washing — either face, lay 1, mount_low_macro, macro lens

- [ ] `POSTWASH.CURL.LEFT.PROFILE` (1/1, required)
      Garment laid front-up and conditioned. Camera at surface level, looking along the
      surface at the left hem edge, rule standing vertically beside the edge so the lift
      off the surface can be read.
      *why:* Edge curl is a vertical lift off the surface and is invisible from overhead; this is the only frame that can measure it.
- [ ] `POSTWASH.CURL.RIGHT.PROFILE` (1/1, required)
      Garment laid front-up and conditioned. Camera at surface level, looking along the
      surface at the right hem edge, rule standing vertically beside the edge so the lift
      off the surface can be read.
      *why:* Edge curl is a vertical lift off the surface and is invisible from overhead; this is the only frame that can measure it.

### After washing — either face, lay 1, mount_macro_fov200, main lens

- [ ] `POSTWASH.WAIST.WAISTBAND_CORNER_L.R1` (1/1, required)
      200 mm field on the junction where the left waistband end, the outseam and the
      front/back panels meet. Waistband top edge across the upper third; >=60 mm of
      outseam below the corner and >=60 mm of waistband inboard; nearest belt loop
      included if present.  [Reproduce the framing of BEFORE.WAIST.WAISTBAND_CORNER_L.R1
      exactly: the app shows it as a ghost overlay, which is a capture aid and never
      evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.WAIST.WAISTBAND_CORNER_L.R1. The waistband corner is the highest-stress junction on the garment and the fixed end-point of the waist circumference; wash shrinkage shows first as pucker at this bar-tack. At the 550 mm waistband framing the bar-tack is a smudge, so without this frame the shrinkage mechanism is unobservable.
- [ ] `POSTWASH.WAIST.WAISTBAND_CORNER_R.R1` (1/1, required)
      Mirror of WAISTBAND_CORNER_L: 200 mm field on the right waistband end / outseam
      junction, >=60 mm of outseam below and >=60 mm of waistband inboard.  [Reproduce the
      framing of BEFORE.WAIST.WAISTBAND_CORNER_R.R1 exactly: the app shows it as a ghost
      overlay, which is a capture aid and never evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.WAIST.WAISTBAND_CORNER_R.R1. Right-hand counterpart; the L/R pair is the only evidence of construction asymmetry at the waist, which otherwise gets read post-wash as differential shrinkage.
- [ ] `POSTWASH.ANOM.EMBROIDERY.R1.I01` (1/1, conditional, n_embroidery > 0)
      200 mm field centred on embroidery instance NN: the whole embroidered area,
      individual stitch penetrations resolvable at the densest point, the stabiliser/denim
      boundary, >=40 mm of plain denim around it, and the nearest seam landmark.
      [Reproduce the framing of BEFORE.ANOM.EMBROIDERY.R1 exactly: the app shows it as a
      ghost overlay, which is a capture aid and never evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.ANOM.EMBROIDERY.R1. Dense embroidery locally stiffens and pre-shrinks the ground fabric, so it is a shrinkage anomaly with a sharp boundary; its threads are also a different fibre that can bleed. Without a before frame at stitch resolution, post-wash puckering around it reads as fabric distortion.
- [ ] `POSTWASH.ANOM.LOGO.R1.I01` (1/1, conditional, n_logos > 0)
      200 mm field centred on logo instance NN (woven tab, printed mark, stamped hardware
      logo): the whole logo with all text legible in the frame's own orientation, its
      attachment to the fabric, >=40 mm of surrounding denim, and the nearest seam
      landmark.  [Reproduce the framing of BEFORE.ANOM.LOGO.R1 exactly: the app shows it
      as a ghost overlay, which is a capture aid and never evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.ANOM.LOGO.R1. Logos are the identity evidence that lets this exact garment be re-identified later, which is what the DATA_ELIGIBILITY exact_garment tri-state demands a written basis for; a verification nobody wrote down is not a verification. They are also small printed or woven elements that visibly degrade in a wash.
- [ ] `POSTWASH.ANOM.PATCH.R1.I01` (1/1, conditional, n_patches > 0)
      200 mm field centred on applied-patch instance NN: the whole patch, its full
      attachment perimeter (stitched, fused or riveted), any lifting at the edges, >=40 mm
      of surrounding denim, and the nearest seam landmark.  [Reproduce the framing of
      BEFORE.ANOM.PATCH.R1 exactly: the app shows it as a ghost overlay, which is a
      capture aid and never evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.ANOM.PATCH.R1. An applied patch is a second fabric with its own shrinkage rate bonded to the garment, and edge lifting is the most common wash failure; a fused patch can also release entirely. Its before-state perimeter is the only reference for judging that.

### After washing — either face, lay 1, mount_overhead_fov350, main lens

- [ ] `POSTWASH.ANOM.PRINT_FADE.R1.I01` (1/1, conditional, n_printed_fade > 0)
      350 mm field centred on fade instance NN (whiskering fan, knee fade, honeycomb): the
      WHOLE fade pattern including its outer boundary where it returns to full-shade
      denim, plus the nearest seam so the pattern is relocatable. A 200 mm field is too
      small for a whisker fan, which is why this ANOM type uses the region tier.
      [Reproduce the framing of BEFORE.ANOM.PRINT_FADE.R1 exactly: the app shows it as a
      ghost overlay, which is a capture aid and never evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.ANOM.PRINT_FADE.R1. Fades are pre-existing shade gradients that a wash redistributes, so they are the strongest confound for any post-wash colour or shade measurement, and their boundaries are also convenient non-seam landmarks. Recorded only at whole-garment scale their boundaries are unresolvable; unrecorded, post-wash shade change is unattributable.

      120 mm field on the busiest 120 mm of the left back pocket's decorative/arcuate
      stitching, including at least one top corner bar-tack. Individual stitch
      penetrations must be countable and the thread's ply visible; the pocket hem seam
      should cross one frame edge for location.  [Reproduce the framing of
      BEFORE.POCKET.STITCHING_BACK_L.R1 exactly: the app shows it as a ghost overlay,
      which is a capture aid and never evidence.]

Stitch pitch and thread condition are the only before/after evidence of thread shrinkage and seam pucker, and thread shrinks at a different rate from the fabric it is sewn into. At the 350 mm pocket framing the stitch line reads as a line, not as stitches, so pitch cannot be counted at all.

      Mirror of STITCHING_BACK_L: 120 mm field on the right back pocket's decorative

      it as a ghost overlay, which is a capture aid and never evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.POCKET.STITCHING_BACK_R.R1. Right-hand counterpart; stitch pitch differences between the two pockets before the wash are the control against which post-wash pucker asymmetry is judged.

      curled patch -- shoot it as it lies and say so). All printed or embossed text
      legible in the frame's own orientation.  [Reproduce the framing of

      capture aid and never evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.WAIST.BRAND_PATCH.R1. A leather or jacron patch is the strongest single-garment identity evidence, it deforms and darkens more than any other component in a wash, and its printed size/lot text is the only independent cross-check on the record's brand_optional and style fields (DENIM_0001 carries style_sku_unknown as a quality flag). Skipping it leaves both identity and the most wash-reactive component unrecorded.
- [ ] `POSTWASH.WAIST.CROTCH_SEAM_BACK.R1` (1/1, required)
      200 mm field, garment back-up, centred on the junction where the back rise seam

      >=60 mm of back rise seam above, all reinforcement stitch rows complete.  [Reproduce
      the framing of BEFORE.WAIST.CROTCH_SEAM_BACK.R1 exactly: the app shows it as a ghost
      overlay, which is a capture aid and never evidence.]

The back crotch is the other end of the rise measurand and the junction that carries the most ply-count change in a wash. Without it the back rise has a start point that cannot be located to better than a few millimetres.

      shows it as a ghost overlay, which is a capture aid and never evidence.]
      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.SEAM.INTERSECT_YOKE_OUTSEAM_L.R1. The yoke/outseam junction is where three seam directions and the most plies meet on the back panel, so it is the back's stiffest point and the anchor that fixes the yoke V against the leg. Without it the yoke angle measured at 550 mm has no resolved end-point.

      *why:* The after-wash half of a matched pair with BEFORE.SEAM.INTERSECT_YOKE_OUTSEAM_R.R1. Right yoke junction; the pair fixes both ends of the yoke seam so the yoke V can be measured as an angle rather than traced as a curve, which is what makes it lay-invariant.

### Offcuts after wash — either face, lay 1, mount_overhead, main lens

- [ ] `OFFCUT_AFTER.LEFT.LABEL` (1/1, required)
      The offcut laid flat with its written label in the same frame, label legible:
      <GARMENT_ID>_OFFCUT_L. Board in frame.
      *why:* Once two offcuts are in two different wash loads, an unlabelled swap is unrecoverable; the label must be photographed with the sample it names.
- [ ] `OFFCUT_AFTER.RIGHT.LABEL` (1/1, required)
      The offcut laid flat with its written label in the same frame, label legible:
      <GARMENT_ID>_OFFCUT_R. Board in frame.
      *why:* Once two offcuts are in two different wash loads, an unlabelled swap is unrecoverable; the label must be photographed with the sample it names.

### Offcuts after wash — BACK up, lay 1, mount_overhead, main lens

- [ ] `OFFCUT_AFTER.LEFT.FACE_BACK` (1/1, required)
      Offcut back-up, flat, whole sample in frame with the board, after washing.
      *why:* The two faces of the offcut fray and curl differently, after washing.
- [ ] `OFFCUT_AFTER.RIGHT.FACE_BACK` (1/1, required)
      Offcut back-up, flat, whole sample in frame with the board, after washing.
      *why:* The two faces of the offcut fray and curl differently, after washing.
